newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Informatics stake sales for liquidity-CEO.
newsitem.headline: Informatics stake sales for liquidity-CEO.

text.p: Directors of Informatics Holdings have sold down their stakes as part of the company's aim to increase market liquidity of its shares, chairman and chief executive officer Wong Tai said on Thursday.

"It is our intention to improve the market liqudity of our shares over a long period of time, so some of these divestments (are) to offer more investors" the opportunity to invest in the company, Wong told reporters after a news conference.
Wong and other directors had been reducing their stakes in the company since last December.
Informatics operates franchises for centres which run information technology training and business education.
"The take-up is mainly by institutions as well as individuals," said Wong.
As of August 15, 1996, Wong held 6.8 million shares or a 2.3 percent stake directly, down from over 13 million shares in July this year.

Other directors who have sold down their stakes include Cheah Hon Kuen, Wong Kock Meng and Ong Boon Kheng. Wong and Cheah have deemed interest in 165 million shares or a 55 percent stake held by investment holding company ASV Holdings Pte Ltd.
"In the past people have been telling us that they can't get the stock, liquidity is no good. Now if you look at the trading volume, I think it is reasonable," Wong said.
He said the free float of Informatics was about 35-40 percent, compared to 20 percent when the company first went public in 1993

On whether there would be further stake reductions by the directors, Wong said: "The idea of having a holding company is to make sure that we have a reasonable control over the company...the rest of it is our individual decisions."
At 0651 GMT on Thursday, Informatics was trading at Singapore $0.645, up S$0.03 on volume of 1.9 million shares.
